name: dolmen

attributes.attribute: called a portal tomb by archaeologists
built thousands of years before the Celts arrived
called the beds of Diarmait and Gráinne in Ireland
slept on a different dolmen each night while eloping
linked to fertility and sexuality by folklore

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The dolmen is a symbolic stone structure. Doorways of stone stand in fields and pasture across the Celtic lands. They rest on rocky hills and in green valleys. The Breton word dolmen means table of stone. Only a giant could eat off most dolmens. Archaeologists prefer the term portal tomb. In Wales the same structures are called cromlechs, from words meaning bent and flat stone. People also call them Druid altars. But they were built thousands of years before the Celts and their priests arrived. Some 6,000 years have passed since stone uprights met huge crossbeams. The builders were so precise that many structures still stand. Burials appear in recesses under the dolmens. This is why archaeologists call them tombs. Yet burials were few compared to the population. Those buried beneath may have been victims of human sacrifice. Or they may have been people of high birth deemed worthy of a special grave. Similar stone structures in the Canadian arctic mark geography and open shamanic doorways. In Ireland these stones are called the beds of Diarmait and Gráinne. The eloping couple was said to sleep on a different one each night. They fled Fionn mac Cumhaill, her angry intended husband. This legend links dolmens to fertility and sexuality. Folklore claims the stones cause sterility, or that they raise the chance of conception.

okr.objective: Record the dolmen as a prehistoric Celtic stone tomb and fertility-linked landmark.
key_results: The Breton word dolmen means table of stone, and archaeologists call it a portal tomb.
The structures predate the Celts and Druids by thousands of years.
Burial recesses under dolmens point to tombs and possible human sacrifice.
In Ireland the stones are called the beds of Diarmait and Gráinne and linked to fertility.
